newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan said seeking 3-yr, 180,000-tonne sugar deal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan said seeking 3-yr, 180,000-tonne sugar deal.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp is expected within weeks to tender for a three-year contract for delivery of 60,000 tonnes of sugar a year, local traders said on Wednesday.
"Taiwan Sugar Corp is preparing to seek a three-year, 60,000-tonnes-per-year sugar supply deal," a trader said.
Taiwan Sugar is likely to hold the invitation-only tender in New York within a few weeks, but exact dates have not been set, the trader added.
A Taiwan Sugar spokesman reached by telephone confirmed that the firm would re-enter the sugar market soon but declined to comment further.
The state-owned company is on track to import 120,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996, industry sources said.
Taiwan Sugar bought two 30,000-tonne shipments of sugar on June 26 in New York, on a cost-and-freight basis, at US$305.50 and US$302 per tonne.
